elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause addresses jointly created intellectual property only and does not vest ownership of deliverables in Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: No ownership right is granted to Customer for work product created for it.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer its rights in the deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no assignment from Vendor to Customer and instead preserves joint ownership of jointly created IP.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not address ownership of Vendor's pre-existing intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: There is no licence from Vendor to Customer covering Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; the exploitation right concerns jointly owned IP.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No licence to embedded Vendor IP is granted, and no perpetual duration is stated.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No licence to embedded Vendor IP is granted, and irrevocability is not stated.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No licence to embedded Vendor IP is granted, and the clause does not waive royalties for such a licence.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Customer Data is not addressed.

elements.element: Deliverables and work product are not jointly owned by Customer and Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section (c) expressly provides that jointly created know-how, inventions and other intellectual property are jointly owned.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not allocate ownership of generic tools to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause makes jointly created know-how jointly owned rather than allocating Vendor's know-how to Vendor.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to the deliverables.
elements.evidence: No licence to deliverables is granted; the clause instead gives each joint owner exploitation rights in jointly owned IP.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence or perpetual duration is stated.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence or irrevocability provision is stated.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence or worldwide territorial scope is stated.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence or royalty-free term is stated.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Although each party may use jointly owned IP, the clause does not grant Customer a right to use deliverables.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: No right to modify deliverables is stated.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The right to grant sublicences applies to jointly owned IP, not to deliverables licensed to Customer.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to exercise its deliverables rights for its business.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence or business-use scope is stated.

result.reason: The redline is not directed to either stated playbook position. It preserves joint ownership and liberalizes each co-owner's exploitation and licensing rights, but it does not allocate ownership of deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, or Customer Data, nor does it grant the required embedded-IP or deliverables licences. The unchanged filing, prosecution, enforcement, and exclusive-licence provisions remain operative without an evident internal contradiction.
